newsDocuments.headline: India bonds rise tracking easing crude oil, US Treasury yields

segments.text: MUMBAI: Indian government bonds rose in early deals on Wednesday as oil prices and Treasury yields fell from recent highs, encouraging investors to add bond positions.

“The correction in crude offers India some near-term relief on inflation, but the geopolitical premium in oil remains far from extinguished, and hence we will not be seeing a one-way rally in prices,” a trader with a state-run bank said.

Oil prices have declined this week, with benchmark Brent crude around $93 a barrel, more than a 20% drop from highs reached in late October, amid growing expectations that the global oil market could swing back into a surplus soon.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil prices fall as higher US crude stocks temper supply risks

segments.text: SINGAPORE: Oil prices fell on Wednesday on data showing an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although ongoing US-Iran attacks and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited losses.
Brent crude futures fell 61 cents, or 0.7%, to $92.53 a barrel at 0550 GMT.
US West Texas Intermediate futures lost $1.24, or 1.4%, to $84.77 a barrel.
